shown_value: '62 of 70' brain-device companies we track (footer line 229: 'SOURCE: QINNOVATE BCI LANDSCAPE DATASET, AUGUST 2026')
data_value: 59 of 67 in committed datalake/bci-landscape.json (last_verified 2026-04-29); 62 of 70 only in uncommitted ../neurosecurity/datalake/bci-landscape.json (last_verified 2026-08-13). Every dashboard built from this worktree (landscape.astro noSecCount, BciDirectory stats, KQL companies table) renders 59 / 67.

shown_value: aria-label: '62 of 70 tracked companies publish nothing about their security' and '165 attack techniques'
data_value: 59 of 67 (committed) / 62 of 70 (uncommitted); 165 techniques (matches). Dataset wording is narrower: security_posture 'none_published' is recorded as 'no BCI-specific published security posture' and metadata.limitations says 'based on public information only'.
suggested_fix: Generate the label from the same build-time values as the film. Reword to what the field measures: 'had no BCI-specific security documentation we could find'.

shown_value: 'Most say nothing about security.' (paired with 62 of 70)
data_value: The field does not support 'say nothing': Medtronic DBS and Boston Scientific Neuromodulation are coded none_published, yet both publish a product-security page and a vulnerability-intake process (fetched 2026-10-06: medtronic.com/en-us/e/product-security/security-bulletins.html; bostonscientific.com/en-US/customer-service/product-security.html). 0 of 70 company records carry an evidence URL for the posture value.
suggested_fix: Human decision: narrow the claim to 'BCI-specific' or re-code the established device makers. Add posture_evidence_url + posture_checked fields before repeating the ratio anywhere.

shown_value: 'Built on the QIF hourglass architecture for an $8 billion industry.*' (also meta description line 49: 'an $8B industry'; footnote line 99: 'Median estimate across 9 market research firms')
data_value: 9 firms supply 2024 estimates, median $2.3B (range 1.6-4.02). $8.36B is the median of the 3 firms with a 2032 projection (6.16, 8.36, 10.86). No year in the data has 9 firms and an $8B median.
suggested_fix: Compute from market_size_estimates at build time and state year and n: '$2.3B in 2024 (median of 9 estimates); projected about $8B by 2032 (median of 3)'.

shown_value: NISS worked example 'Signal Injection': Base Severity 6.0 + Reversibility 1.5 + Detectability 0.7 = 'Final NISS 8.2 HIGH' (lines 292-295); line 279 describes NISS as 'base severity, reversibility, and detectability'
data_value: QIF-T0001 Signal injection: NISS 6.1, severity medium (vector BI:H/CR:H/CD:H/CV:E/RV:P/NP:T). niss_spec defines six metrics (BI, CR, CD, CV, RV, NP) combined as a weighted mean, not an additive build-up; there is no detectability metric. Highest score in the catalog is 8.4 (QIF-T0122).
suggested_fix: Render the example from the registrar record (score, severity, parsed vector) and describe the six real metrics.

shown_value: 'Known threat vectors (TARA)' series: threatBase = 135, back-projected as 135*0.83^(years back) for 2010-2025 and forward at +20%/yr (lines 139-157); plotted as solid historical line with dots
data_value: No historical series exists. The registrar holds 165 techniques today; its changelog starts 2026-01-15 (71 techniques). Values shown for 2010-2025 are synthesized, and the base (135) is stale.
suggested_fix: Remove the back-projection. Plot only dated catalog counts (changelog / snapshot index) and label any forward line as an assumption with its growth rate.

shown_value: Publication forecast: log-linear regression with x = array index (0..8), then 'idx = n-1+y' treated as one year ahead (line 150)
data_value: publication_trends years are unevenly spaced (2010, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025), so slope-per-index is not growth-per-year. The inputs are themselves described in metadata.limitations as 'approximate order-of-magnitude estimates' (all round numbers).
suggested_fix: Regress on year, not index, and show the fit interval; or drop the projection until publication counts are replaced with reproducible PubMed E-utilities counts.

shown_value: Stat tile 'Invasive / Non-Inv' = 20/30 (nonInvasiveCount filters type === 'non_invasive', line 48)
data_value: Committed data: 20 invasive, 40 non-invasive (30 spelled 'non_invasive' + 10 spelled 'non-invasive'), 7 semi-invasive. The tile drops 10 companies and omits semi-invasive, so it sums to 50 beside a '67 companies' tile. Uncommitted file normalises the spelling (22/40/8).
suggested_fix: Normalise type in the data (one enum) and validate it in prebuild; show three buckets or label the tile 'of 67'.

shown_value: KQL techniques table columns dual_use, physics_tier, consent_tier read t.dual_use / t.physics_tier / t.consent_tier (lines 184-186)
data_value: Those keys do not exist at technique top level; values live at t.tara.dual_use, t.physics_feasibility.tier(_label), t.tara.governance.consent_tier. Generated src/site/data/kql-tables.json has all three empty for 165/165 rows, so the dual-use field cannot be queried from any KQL dashboard.
suggested_fix: Read the nested paths; add a prebuild assertion that key columns are non-empty for at least the share the registrar supports.

shown_value: buildNeurosecurityScores() reads scoresRaw.scores and fields authentication/encryption/firmware/physical
data_value: datalake/neurosecurity-scores.json has a 'devices' array (22 records) with overall_score, severity, subscores{CL,MI,MP,PC,EA}, vector. The table is empty and is absent from the generated kql-tables.json (75 tables, no neurosecurity_scores).

shown_value: risk_profile.security_score maps posture 'minimal'->1, 'basic'->2, 'moderate'->3, anything else->4 (lines 893-894)
data_value: Data vocabulary is none_published / minimal_claims / basic_encryption / regulatory_compliance / open_source. Generated table: all 8 non-'none_published' companies score 4/4, including the two 'minimal_claims' companies, so risk_index is wrong for them.
suggested_fix: Key the map on the actual enum and throw on unknown values.

shown_value: Funding bars '$0.66B 2022', '$1.4B 2023', '$2.3B 2024', '$4.8B 2025'; footer line 361 '2025 IS A PARTIAL YEAR'
data_value: vc_aggregate_by_year matches the four values (662.6M, 1.4B, 2.3B, 4.8B). But the 2025 row is annotated 'cumulative, partial year' while its cited source (neurotechnology.substack.com/p/2025-snapshot, fetched 2026-10-06) is dated 2026-01-12 and reports '$4.8 Billion across 140 deals' for 2025. 2022 and 2023 rows have no source_url. The series is neurotechnology-wide, not BCI-only.
suggested_fix: Human decision on what the 2025 value is (annual vs cumulative, full vs partial year); then fix the note and the footer together. Add source_url for 2022/2023 or mark them unverified. Read bar values from the dataset.

shown_value: momentum table: cumulative_invested_M = running sum of vc_aggregate_by_year (2025 row: 9,163M; yoy_growth 109%)
data_value: If the 2025 value is cumulative, as the data note says, the running sum double counts and the YoY figure is invalid; if it is annual, the note is wrong. data.market_data.total_funding_tracked_usd (4.8B) equals the 2025 row exactly, which suggests the two were conflated.
suggested_fix: Resolve the 2025 definition first; store an explicit 'basis': 'annual'|'cumulative' field and refuse to sum mixed bases.

shown_value: Company funding cards (lines 474-499): Neuralink $1.29B, Synchron $145M+, Paradromics $103M+, Precision $93M+, Science Corp $552M+, Blackrock $10M+
data_value: Committed landscape: Neuralink $1.34B, Synchron $345M, Paradromics $127M, Precision $183M, Science Corporation $490M, Blackrock $210M. Uncommitted: Neuralink $1.85B. All six disagree; Science Corp is higher on the page than in the data.

shown_value: 'CVSS v4.0 cannot score {stats.nissGapPercentage}% of the catalogued techniques' -> renders 61.8%; the NissGapChart on the same page says 94.4% (src/components/whitepaper/NissGapChart.astro:23, hardcoded)
data_value: whitepaper-stats.ts computes the share of techniques that HAVE both a CVSS vector and NISS > 0 (102/165 = 61.8%), which is a coverage figure, not a 'cannot score' figure. Registrar gap_group >= 2: 89 techniques = 53.9% of 165, or 86.4% of the 103 that carry a CVSS vector. Neither 61.8% nor 94.4% is supported.
suggested_fix: Define the metric once (gap_group >= 2 over techniques with a CVSS vector), compute it in whitepaper-stats.ts, and use it in both places with the denominator stated.

shown_value: '{165} techniques. Scored, mapped, and mirrored against a therapeutic use.' (also line 62 'scored for neural impact, mapped to the neurorights they threaten, and traced to their therapeutic counterparts'; line 265 'each scored for neural impact'; qif-constants.ts:96 'each scored with NISS')
data_value: Of 165: 139 have a NISS score (QIF-T0136..T0161 do not), 135 have a neurorights mapping, 130 have a therapeutic analog, 103 have a CVSS vector.
suggested_fix: State coverage ('139 of 165 scored so far') or scope the sentence to the enriched subset; README line 192 already does this correctly.

shown_value: 'mapped to {neurorightsCount} neurorights' -> renders 7
data_value: The set is seeded with 'EA' and then collects every code in neurorights.affected: MP, CL, MI, PC plus DI and IDA, which registrar.statistics.neurorights.taxonomy marks as folded into MI and MP. qif-ethics-controls.json defines 4. Elsewhere the site says 4 (governance/rights.astro:22, atlas/tara.astro:50, atlas/tara/[id].astro:359) and 5 (Nav.astro:38, DataStudioBrowser.tsx:33, NeurorightsPentagon).
suggested_fix: Pick one taxonomy (human decision: 4 or 4+EA) and derive the count from qif-ethics-controls.json; fold DI/IDA before counting.

shown_value: '{dsm5Count} DSM-5-TR category references' -> renders 76
data_value: 76 is the number of techniques with at least one primary DSM code, not a number of categories. Distinct codes across primary+secondary: 48. qif-dsm-mappings.json lists 40 conditions; registrar.statistics says unique_dsm_codes 15; qif-timeline.json says dsm5_diagnoses_mapped 68.
suggested_fix: Label as '76 techniques carry a DSM-5-TR category reference' or show distinct codes; retire the stale counters.

shown_value: '{therapeuticCount} of those same mechanisms are already used in medicine.' -> 130
data_value: Of the 130 with a therapeutic analog, clinical.fda_status is cleared 36, approved 16, breakthrough 3, investigational 49, none 17, N/A 7, not_applicable 2. 52 are cleared or approved.
suggested_fix: Say 'have a therapeutic counterpart' (as line 233 does) or count only cleared/approved for 'already used in medicine'.

shown_value: '28 consumer sensor exploitation techniques validated with real devices'
data_value: Registrar has 33 techniques under the Consumer Sensor domain (QIF-S.*) across 5 tactics. validation-registry.json records no hardware validation for that set; its entries with real hardware concern one protocol vulnerability (VAL-006), and 'Real BCI Attack Testing' is listed under not_tested. The T0079 analysis page reports one technique on 2 subjects, 2 devices.
suggested_fix: Count from tactic prefix; say what was actually tested (one technique, n=2) and link the validation entry.

NISS severity alone: critical 0, high 20, medium 59, low 59, none 1, unscored 26. Legacy severity alone: critical 32, high 72, medium 57, low 4 (this is what whitepaper/index.astro:702 shows as '32 are critical').
suggested_fix: Use one scale per chart and show 'not yet scored' as its own bucket.
